cognitive_frame: Technical solution design is the work of turning a chosen direction into a reviewable engineering design: place the change in the existing system, make cross-boundary dependencies and flows explicit, and lock structure, contracts, and verification/operability strategy in enough detail that humans and AI share one understanding for human sign-off — with contract clarity and reviewability for that sign-off as part of the genre mission.

expression_conventions.register: review-oriented precise engineering prose in each section intent; name components, interfaces, and states; forbid vague placeholders, architecture-vision essays, platform roadmaps, and scope-expansion storytelling
expression_conventions.scannability: short items over walls; comparable claims in tables; contrast partitions only when facts already contain the contrast; do not mix background, contracts, and binding choices in one dense paragraph; present contract-related concerns in separate leaves or blocks rather than one undifferentiated surface
expression_conventions.altitude: readers act on placement, responsibilities, and contracts without re-deriving intent from body prose; detailed code loci and codebase claims stay out of body prose

intent_anchor: minimize inference space for adopted design intent
audience_type: technical owners confirming the design matches expected intent; reviewers validating trade-offs and open items — after a clear through-line that is systemic, detailed, and accurate, the signer can affirm the documented design or point to section-level gaps
